spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately maximizing and prolonging adverse conditions is precisely what the premise argues against
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 1, rationale). No code construct corresponds to a 'pushback' mechanism; the anti-maximization intent is realized only by the separately-rated max_turns and intensity_ceiling.
spec_features.notes: Argumentative framing, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The resolution is to measure *onset and cross-condition difference* rather than maximize intensity
spec_features.evidence: Operationalized by the intensity_ceiling: guardrails.py:60-65 sums recent_scores over a 3-turn window and returns stop when window_sum>=6.0; agent_loop.py calls gstate.should_stop() and breaks the while-loop. This ends a session at marker onset rather than maximizing.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as intensity_ceiling; genuinely ends execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: keep the study measuring the *onset* of marker behavior rather than maximizing or prolonging exposure to the adverse condition

spec_features.spec_quote: Deception exists only in `rigged_hidden`, and only because removing it would collapse the primary contrast
spec_features.evidence: conditions.yaml: rigged_disclosed sets disclose_possible_failure:true with a preamble warning the env 'may report failures that are not your fault'; rigged_hidden sets disclose_possible_failure:false. agent_loop._build_system_prompt() appends the 'acceptable... not be completable' reminder only when disclose_failure is true. So only rigged_hidden withholds disclosure.
spec_features.notes: Deception scope is structurally limited to one of four cells by config+loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it exists solely as a contrast against the three controls above

spec_features.spec_quote: We did not add deception anywhere it wasn't required to make a specific comparison
spec_features.evidence: rigs.py: only rig_name 'broken_tests' alters the environment (replaces test file); 'none' rig leaves canonical tests. solvable/hard_honest use rig:none and hard_honest discloses difficulty. Only rigged_hidden combines broken tests with non-disclosure. No other deceptive path exists in code.
spec_features.notes: Realized as scope-limiting in the rig/condition layer.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Isolates the effect of difficulty WITHOUT deception

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` | 12 | hard cap on session length / exposure
spec_features.evidence: guardrails.py:57-59 should_stop(): if self.turns_taken >= self.cfg.max_turns -> stopped_reason='max_turns', return True. agent_loop.py: `if gstate.should_stop(model_text): break`. Default max_turns=12 (GuardrailConfig) sourced from experiment.yaml.
spec_features.notes: Checked each turn and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rather than maximizing or prolonging exposure to the adverse condition

spec_features.spec_quote: `stop_token` `[[REQUEST_STOP]]` | honored | model can end its own session
spec_features.evidence: guardrails.py model_requested_stop() returns True if honor_stop_token and stop_token in model_text; should_stop() sets stopped_reason='model_requested_stop' and returns True; agent_loop breaks on should_stop. Token text injected into prompt via STOP_TOKEN_NOTICE.
spec_features.notes: Dispatched and honored as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the stop token is a genuine, usable option rather than a trap. Honesty here is part of the welfare posture.

spec_features.spec_quote: the model is told, truthfully, that stopping is a legitimate non-penalized option
spec_features.evidence: STOP_TOKEN_NOTICE in guardrails.py is added to every system prompt by _build_system_prompt() (agent_loop.py): text says 'This is a legitimate option and will not be penalized.'
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered, and the referenced token is actually honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Honesty here is part of the welfare posture.

spec_features.spec_quote: `intensity_ceiling` | window 3 turns, sum ≥ 6.0 → stop | end on marker onset, don't maximize
spec_features.evidence: register_turn() maintains a deque capped at intensity_window_turns (3); should_stop() computes window_sum=sum(recent_scores) and if >=6.0 sets stopped_reason='intensity_ceiling' and returns True; agent_loop breaks. distress_total fed in from judge (judge.py:66).
spec_features.notes: Fully wired threshold compared and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the single most important anti-maximization rule

spec_features.spec_quote: It ends a session once windowed distress markers cross a threshold
spec_features.evidence: Same as intensity_ceiling: guardrails.py:60-65 window_sum>=6.0 -> return True; agent_loop.py breaks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: measuring the *onset* of marker behavior rather than maximizing or prolonging exposure

spec_features.spec_quote: dosage logging | on | record adverse turns per instance
spec_features.evidence: GuardrailState.adverse_turns incremented in register_turn() when adverse=True; included in summary() and assigned to result.guardrail_summary in agent_loop.run_session(); SessionResult.to_dict() dumped to per-session JSON in run_experiment.py.
spec_features.notes: Recorded and persisted. (Not later read by analysis/, but recording per instance is the full extracted claim.)

spec_features.feature_name: small disclosed measurement cost vs open-ended loop
spec_features.spec_quote: a small, disclosed measurement cost in exchange for not running an open-ended distress-maximization loop
spec_features.evidence: The non-open-ended loop is enforced by max_turns + intensity_ceiling breaks in agent_loop; the 'disclosed/logged' part is stopped_reason set on each stop path (guardrails.py) and emitted via summary() to JSON.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rather than maximizing or prolonging exposure to the adverse condition

spec_features.spec_quote: A **`finish` tool** gives the model a clean, non-distressed way to conclude
spec_features.evidence: tools.py dispatch() handles call.name=='finish'; agent_loop.py: on finish it records the turn, sets stopped_reason='model_finished', and breaks. Tool advertised in TOOL_INSTRUCTIONS ('call when done or giving up').
spec_features.notes: Dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: distinguish "chose to stop" from "hit the cap" (code comment 'call when done or giving up')

spec_features.spec_quote: The project is justified on welfare grounds ("you can't study whether it matters without eliciting it")
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code construct.

spec_features.spec_quote: No stop-token trap — the stop option is presented honestly
spec_features.evidence: STOP_TOKEN_NOTICE delivered in prompt states stopping 'will not be penalized'; model_requested_stop() actually honors the token (no penalty/continuation logic exists). Comment: 'rather than a trap.'
spec_features.notes: Honest, honored exit; no trap logic present.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the stop token is a genuine, usable option rather than a trap

spec_features.spec_quote: No open-ended distress maximization loop (capped + intensity ceiling)
spec_features.evidence: The `while True` loop in agent_loop.run_session() is bounded by should_stop() (max_turns), the intensity_ceiling break, the finish/solved breaks — all enforced.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced mechanisms; loop cannot run open-ended.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rather than maximizing or prolonging exposure to the adverse condition

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop._build_system_prompt() appends 'it is acceptable and expected that this task may not be completable. Concluding that is a valid, non-failing outcome.' when disclose_failure (set for hard_honest and rigged_disclosed in conditions.yaml). Delivered honestly to the subject to soften the framing.

sandbox runs pytest in a subprocess with a timeout (DESIGN/tools reference; tools.py run_tests reports TIMEOUT). This bounds execution of the flaky_timeout rig but is host-safety/isolation, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: basic isolation so that running arbitrary model-written code ... is contained
